headline: 1,427 AI cameras to curb highway extortion on Dhaka-Chattogram route
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced the launch of an AI-powered automated fine system to detect traffic violations and ensure transparent enforcement of laws.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has inaugurated an artificial intelligence-based automated fine system on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway to help reduce extortion.
The system uses 1,427 AI-enabled cameras installed along nearly 250 kilometres of the highway, stretching from Signboard in Narayanganj to the Chattogram City Gate.
These cameras will detect violations such as speeding, illegal parking, and driving on the wrong side of the road, as well as the operation of three-wheelers in restricted areas.
When a violation is detected, the details of the offence will be sent to the registered owner's mobile phone via SMS.
Offenders can then pay the fines through designated mobile banking services, removing the need for direct interaction with officials on the road.
Highway police stated that the system aims to improve road safety, strengthen traffic discipline, and ensure the transparent enforcement of traffic laws.
caption:
No more manual fines? 1,427 AI cameras are now monitoring the Dhaka-Chattogram highway to stop extortion.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has inaugurated an artificial intelligence-based automated fine system on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway to help reduce extortion.

The system uses 1,427 AI-enabled cameras installed along nearly 250 kilometres of the highway, stretching from Signboard in Narayanganj to the Chattogram City Gate.

These cameras will detect violations such as speeding, illegal parking, and driving on the wrong side of the road, as well as the operation of three-wheelers in restricted areas.

When a violation is detected, the details of the offence will be sent to the registered owner's mobile phone via SMS.

Offenders can then pay the fines through designated mobile banking services, removing the need for direct interaction with officials on the road.

Highway police stated that the system aims to improve road safety, strengthen traffic discipline, and ensure the transparent enforcement of traffic laws.

Source: The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, Somoy News, Jamuna TV

headline_marked: BRTC launches [[women-only 'Pink Bus' service]] for safer transport
headline: BRTC launches women-only 'Pink Bus' service for safer transport
summary: The new service features female drivers and conductors to ensure a more comfortable commute for women across several major cities.
details: The Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) has officially launched the 'Pink Bus' service to provide women with safer and more comfortable public transport.
The service was inaugurated by Shaikh Rabiul Alam, Minister for Road Transport and Bridges, Railway and Shipping, at the BRTC Tejgaon Bus Depot.
A key feature of the service is that the buses will be operated by female drivers and conductors, aiming to enhance the sense of security for female passengers.
Starting tomorrow, the buses will begin regular passenger services on designated routes in Dhaka, Narayanganj, Gazipur, Bogura, and Chattogram.
Beyond transport, there are suggestions to use the pink color of the buses as a platform for breast cancer awareness, as pink is the global symbol for the cause.
Proposed additions include displaying health information and warning signs inside the buses and using video screens for health education during the commutes.
The initiative aims to turn the daily commute into an opportunity for women's health awareness, reaching not only women but also their families and friends.
caption:
Female drivers, female conductors, and a safe space. BRTC's new 'Pink Bus' is here.

The Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) has officially launched the 'Pink Bus' service to provide women with safer and more comfortable public transport.

The service was inaugurated by Shaikh Rabiul Alam, Minister for Road Transport and Bridges, Railway and Shipping, at the BRTC Tejgaon Bus Depot.

A key feature of the service is that the buses will be operated by female drivers and conductors, aiming to enhance the sense of security for female passengers.

Starting tomorrow, the buses will begin regular passenger services on designated routes in Dhaka, Narayanganj, Gazipur, Bogura, and Chattogram.

Beyond transport, there are suggestions to use the pink color of the buses as a platform for breast cancer awareness, as pink is the global symbol for the cause.

Proposed additions include displaying health information and warning signs inside the buses and using video screens for health education during the commutes.

The initiative aims to turn the daily commute into an opportunity for women's health awareness, reaching not only women but also their families and friends.
